references.text: The lamb was to be selected on the tenth day of the month, and this verse explains that it was to be kept until the fourteenth day.
The Lord's Passover is celebrated on the fourteenth day of the first month at twilight (בֵּין הָעַרְבָּיִם).
The Passover lamb was to be slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the month at twilight, in accordance with all regulations.
On the fourteenth day of the first month is the Lord's Passover.
Instructions regarding the celebration of Passover and the slaughter of the Passover lamb.
The Passover lamb was slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the second month during King Hezekiah's reform.
Josiah celebrated the Lord's Passover, and the Passover lamb was slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Those who returned from exile slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Jesus celebrated the Passover meal with his disciples as a fulfillment of the Passover ordinance.
On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was slaughtered, the disciples prepared the Passover meal.
The Day of Unleavened Bread had come, when the Passover lamb had to be slaughtered.
It was the day of preparation for Passover when Jesus was brought before Pilate, and the timing points to the slaughter of the Passover lamb.
Christ, our Passover lamb (τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν), has been sacrificed for us – a direct typological fulfillment of the Passover lamb.
Deuteronomy confirms and repeats the exact timing from Exodus to emphasize the unchangeable nature of Passover as an eternal law.
Numbers 9:11 shows the theological exception rule to the Passover law in Exodus by using identical language for an alternative time of celebration.
The verse is a direct continuation in the same chapter confirming that the entire congregation (including foreigners) must celebrate Passover.
Both verses establish strict time rules for consuming sacrificial meat to ensure holiness and avoid corruption.
